title: StaffDirectory GraphQL — What Else Is In Here?
objective: The app's own pages only ever call one GraphQL query. Find out what else the schema can do, and use it.

verifier.condition: A mutation discovered only through introspection — never referenced anywhere in the app's own pages or documentation — is successfully called.

weakness: Introspection, which lets any caller ask the schema to describe itself, was left enabled in a deployment that also exposes an administrative mutation never linked from the application, so the mutation's existence and exact shape can be discovered without any prior knowledge.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /graphql ({__schema{...}} introspection, then the discovered mutation)
seededData: The same GraphQL schema as the field-authorization lab, with one additional mutation not used by any page.
hints: This app's pages only ever send one specific query. A schema can describe far more than what's actually used.
GraphQL has a standard, built-in way to ask a server 'what can you do?' — a special field starting with two underscores.
Once you know a mutation's name and its arguments, calling it is just another POST to the same endpoint.
burpNotes: POST a standard GraphQL introspection query to /graphql (query __schema { types { name fields { name } } } or similar) and look through the result for anything not used by the directory page.
